content.title: About
content.content: Cookies and macaroons are small sweet baked goods made from a dough of flour, sugar, eggs, and fats. Macaroons often feature a crisp outer shell with a soft, sometimes slightly chewy interior, and come in a variety of flavors and fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest cookie recipes date back to ancient Rome, where they were baked with honey and nuts.
The word “macaroon” derives from the Italian “maccherone,” meaning “small pasta,” because the original shape resembled tiny pasta shells.
In France, macaroons became popular in the 19th century thanks to nuns at a convent in Lyon who began selling them.
There are two main types of macaroons: French (made from meringue, almond flour, and sugar) and Italian (a light sponge‑like cake).
Cookies are often used as a base for dessert tarts and cheesecakes.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Contains almond flour
items.content: Many macaroons are made with almond flour, which is rich in vitamin E and heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Sugar and spices such as cinnamon can contribute antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: The sweet taste stimulates serotonin production, which can temporarily lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Almond flour in macaroons may trigger allergic reactions in people with nut allergies.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Some commercial cookies contain partially hydrogenated oils, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies and macaroons can be enjoyed as a standalone treat, paired with tea, coffee, or milk, used as a crust for cakes, or added to ice cream and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies and macaroons in an airtight container at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain the crisp exterior.
